inlines.text: On a particular day, Dr Rosanna starts seeing patients at 8:30 am and finishes by 5:30 pm.

From 8:30 am to 5:30 pm is $9$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}

\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Divide by $60$ to convert minutes to hours. Only the operation is required.
$$15\text{ min}=(15\div60)\text{ h}$$

There are $60$ minutes in an hour.
$$\begin{align*}200\text{ min}&=(200\div60)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ seconds in a minute.
$$\begin{align*}300\text{ s}&=(300\div60)\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ seconds in a minute.
$$\begin{align*}193\text{ min}&=(193\times60)\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ minutes in an hour.
$$\begin{align*}4.5\text{ h}&=(4.5\times60)\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

There are $60$ minutes in an hour.
$$\begin{align*}635\text{ min}&=(635\div60)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

Convert the hours to minutes, then add the remaining minutes.
$$\begin{align*}4\text{ h }37\text{ min}&=(4\times60+37)\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

Convert the minutes to seconds, then add the remaining seconds.
$$\begin{align*}47\text{ min }12\text{ s}&=(47\times60+12)\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

Convert the days to hours, then add the remaining hours.
$$\begin{align*}5\text{ days }17\text{ h}&=(5\times24+17)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

There are $24$ hours in a day.
$$\begin{align*}100\text{ h}&=(100\div24)\text{ days}\end{align*}$$

There are $7$ days in a week and $24$ hours in a day.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ week}&=7\text{ days}\\1\text{ week}&=(7\times24)\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

There are $24$ hours in a day.
$$\begin{align*}10\,000\text{ h}&=(10\,000\div24)\text{ days}\end{align*}$$

children.prompt:

How long would it take her to type a 500-word essay?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{75\text{ words}}{1\text{ min}}&=\frac{500\text{ words}}{x\text{ min}}\end{align*}$$
Take reciprocals of both sides.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1\text{ min}}{75\text{ words}}&=\frac{x\text{ min}}{500\text{ words}}\\\frac{1}{75}\times500\text{ min}&=x\text{ min}\\\frac{20}{3}\text{ min}&=x\text{ min}\\6.\dot{6}\text{ min}&=x\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

Let $x$ be the number of days. Convert the total practice time to minutes, then use equivalent rates.

classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate additive reasoning in a recipe and calculate the correct quantity using equivalent rates.

inlines.text: The recipe requires: 300 g cream cheese, 125 mL thickened cream.
Cream cheese only comes in 250 g packs so he bought 2 packs: 500 grams of cream cheese.
Mr Ding thought “If I’m increasing the amount of cream cheese by 200 g, then I should increase the amount of thickened cream by 200 mL, so I need 325 mL”

children.label: a
children.prompt: Describe what would happen to his cheesecake if he did this.

inlines.text: He is less-than-doubling the cream cheese but more-than-doubling the cream. It would be too runny.

answer.worked: The cream cheese is multiplied by $\frac{500}{300}=\frac{5}{3}$, while the cream is multiplied by $\frac{325}{125}=\frac{13}{5}$. The cream has increased by a greater factor, so there is too much cream relative to the cheese. The cheesecake would be too runny.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How much thickened cream should he use for 500 g of cream cheese? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the amount of thickened cream in mL.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{300\text{ g cheese}}{125\text{ mL cream}}&=\frac{500\text{ g cheese}}{x\text{ mL cream}}\end{align*}$$
Take the reciprocal of both sides.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{125\text{ mL cream}}{300\text{ g cheese}}&=\frac{x\text{ mL cream}}{500\text{ g cheese}}\\x&=\frac{125\times500}{300}\\x&=\frac{625}{3}\\x&\approx208.33\end{align*}$$
He should use approximately $208.33\text{ mL}$ of thickened cream.

children.label: b

$$\begin{align*}\text{Number of bags}&=\frac{120\text{ kg}}{20\text{ kg/bag}}\\&=6\text{ bags}\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: What area could be fertilised with $1\text{ t}$ of fertiliser?

$1\text{ t}=1000\text{ kg}$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1\text{ m}^2}{0.2\text{ kg}}&=\frac{x\text{ m}^2}{1000\text{ kg}}\\x&=\frac{1000}{0.2}\\x&=5000\end{align*}$$
The area is $5000\text{ m}^2$.

content.prompt: A car used 30 litres of fuel to travel 105 km. The fuel tank of the car has a capacity of 50 litres. Can the car complete a 180 km journey without refuelling? Give the fuel required to 1 decimal place.

answer.short: No. The journey requires approximately $51.4\text{ L}$, which exceeds the $50\text{ L}$ tank capacity.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{30\text{ L}}{105\text{ km}}&=\frac{x\text{ L}}{180\text{ km}}\\x&=\frac{30\times180}{105}\\x&=\frac{360}{7}\\x&\approx51.4\end{align*}$$
The journey requires approximately $51.4\text{ L}$. Since this exceeds the $50\text{ L}$ tank capacity, the car cannot complete the journey without refuelling.

children.prompt: How many times will a heart beat in a lifetime of 80 years?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\frac{70\text{ beats}}{1\text{ min}}&=\frac{70\text{ beats}}{(1\div60\div24\div365)\text{ year}}\\\frac{70\text{ beats}}{1\text{ min}}&=\frac{36\,792\,000\text{ beats}}{1\text{ year}}\\\frac{36\,792\,000\text{ beats}}{1\text{ year}}&=\frac{x\text{ beats}}{80\text{ years}}\\x&=36\,792\,000\times80\\x&=2\,943\,360\,000\text{ beats}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How long will it take for a heart to beat 1 million times? Give your answer in days, to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{70\text{ beats}}{1\text{ min}}&=\frac{1\,000\,000\text{ beats}}{x\text{ min}}\end{align*}$$
Take the reciprocal of both sides.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1\text{ min}}{70\text{ beats}}&=\frac{x\text{ min}}{1\,000\,000\text{ beats}}\\x&=\frac{1\,000\,000}{70}\text{ min}\\x&=\frac{100\,000}{7}\text{ min}\\x&=\frac{100\,000}{7\times60}\text{ h}\\x&=\frac{100\,000}{7\times60\times24}\text{ days}\\x&\approx9.9\text{ days}\end{align*}$$
The intermediate times are approximately $14\,285.7$ min and $238.1$ h; the calculation uses unrounded values.

How many millilitres of soft drink contain 4.5 grams of sugar?

answer.worked:
Let the volume be $x$ mL. Since $1\text{ L}=1000\text{ mL}$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{90\text{ g}}{1000\text{ mL}}&=\frac{4.5\text{ g}}{x\text{ mL}}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1000\text{ mL}}{90\text{ g}}&=\frac{x\text{ mL}}{4.5\text{ g}}\\x&=\frac{1000\times4.5}{90}\\x&=50\end{align*}$$
The volume is $50\text{ mL}$.

inlines.text: Ruth’s tropical fish are breeding at a rate of 8 new fry every 2 days per female fish.
If Ruth has a total of 9 female fish, then how long will it take them to birth a total of 90 new fry?

answer.worked:
For each female fish, $8\div2=4$ new fry per day.

For 9 female fish, $9\times4=36$ new fry per day.

Let $x$ be the time in days. Using equivalent rates and taking reciprocals:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{36}{1}&=\frac{90}{x}\\\frac{1}{36}&=\frac{x}{90}\\90\times\frac{1}{36}&=x\\x&=2.5\end{align*}$$

It takes $2.5$ days.

inlines.text: A river is flowing downstream at a rate of 1 km/h.
In still water Portia can swim at a rate of 2 km/h.
Portia dives into the river and swims downstream, then turns around and swims back to the starting point, taking 0.5 hours in total.

answer.short: $0.75\text{ km}=750\text{ m}$ total. The downstream and upstream speeds are $3\text{ km/h}$ and $1\text{ km/h}$; each leg is $0.375\text{ km}$.
answer.worked:
Downstream speed: $2+1=3\text{ km/h}$.

Upstream speed: $2-1=1\text{ km/h}$.

Let the distance swum downstream be $d$ km. The return distance is also $d$ km.

Time downstream + time upstream $=0.5$ h. Using $t=\dfrac{d}{s}$:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{d}{3}+\frac{d}{1}&=0.5\\\frac{4d}{3}&=0.5\\4d&=1.5\\d&=0.375\end{align*}$$

Each leg is $0.375\text{ km}$. Total distance swum:

$$\begin{align*}2d&=2\times0.375\text{ km}\\&=0.75\text{ km}\\&=750\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

The distance from Broken Hill to Tibooburra is 360 km. A motorist travels from Broken Hill to Tibooburra at a mean speed of 90 km/h and returns at a mean speed of 60 km/h.
What is the average speed of the motorist for the whole journey?

answer.worked:
Using $t=\dfrac{d}{s}$ for each stage:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\text{out}}&=\frac{360}{90}\\t_{\text{out}}&=4\text{ h}\\t_{\text{return}}&=\frac{360}{60}\\t_{\text{return}}&=6\text{ h}\\d_{\text{total}}&=360+360\\d_{\text{total}}&=720\text{ km}\\t_{\text{total}}&=4+6\\t_{\text{total}}&=10\text{ h}\\s_{\text{average}}&=\frac{d_{\text{total}}}{t_{\text{total}}}\\s_{\text{average}}&=\frac{720}{10}\\s_{\text{average}}&=72\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

Marco's time:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\text{Marco}}&=\frac{d}{s}\\t_{\text{Marco}}&=\frac{30}{10}\\t_{\text{Marco}}&=3\text{ h}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
Shari travels at 50 km/h for 10 km. For the next 10 km she wants to drive fast enough to make her average speed 100 km/h over the 20 km trip.

Advise Shari about reaching this average speed.

answer.short: For 100 km/h over 20 km, she must complete the whole journey in 12 minutes. She has already spent 12 minutes to travel 10 km at 50 km/h, so it is impossible.
answer.worked:
Required time for the whole journey:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\text{total}}&=\frac{d_{\text{total}}}{s_{\text{average}}}\\t_{\text{total}}&=\frac{20}{100}\\t_{\text{total}}&=0.2\text{ h}\\t_{\text{total}}&=12\text{ min}\end{align*}$$
Time already spent:
$$\begin{align*}t_{\text{first}}&=\frac{d_{\text{first}}}{s_{\text{first}}}\\t_{\text{first}}&=\frac{10}{50}\\t_{\text{first}}&=0.2\text{ h}\\t_{\text{first}}&=12\text{ min}\end{align*}$$
She has already used all 12 minutes allowed for the whole journey. The remaining 10 km takes additional time at any finite speed, so an average speed of 100 km/h is impossible.

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Time taken} &= 10\text{ am}-8\text{ am}=2\text{ h}\\\text{Speed} &= \frac{7\text{ km}}{2\text{ h}}\\\text{Speed} &= 3.5\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Time taken} &= 11{:}30\text{ am}-10{:}30\text{ am}=1\text{ h}\\\text{Speed} &= \frac{(12-7)\text{ km}}{1\text{ h}}\\\text{Speed} &= 5\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: during the return trip?

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\text{Time taken} &= 3{:}30\text{ pm}-12{:}30\text{ pm}=3\text{ h}\\\text{Speed} &= \frac{12\text{ km}}{3\text{ h}}\\\text{Speed} &= 4\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total distance} &= 12+12=24\text{ km}\\\text{Total time} &= 7\text{ h }30\text{ min}=7.5\text{ h}\\\text{Average speed} &= \frac{24\text{ km}}{7.5\text{ h}}\\\text{Average speed} &= 3.2\text{ km/h}\end{aligned}$$

The total time includes both stops.

inlines.text: Michelle can complete a landscaping job in 6 days and Danielle can complete the job in 4 days.
Working together, in how many days could they complete the job?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Combined rate}&=\frac{1\text{ job}}{6\text{ days}}+\frac{1\text{ job}}{4\text{ days}}\\\text{Combined rate}&=\frac{5\text{ jobs}}{12\text{ days}}\\\text{Combined rate}&=\frac{1\text{ job}}{\frac{12}{5}\text{ days}}\\\text{Time}&=2.4\text{ days}\end{align*}$$
Convert the fractional day to hours and minutes.
$$\begin{align*}0.4\text{ day}&=0.4\times24\text{ hours}=9.6\text{ hours}\\0.6\text{ hour}&=0.6\times60\text{ minutes}=36\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$
They will take **2.4 days**, or **2 days 9 hours 36 minutes**.

Mr Ding, Ms Fu and Mrs Falconer are organising the maths textbooks in the 8 bookshelves in the staffroom. Mr Ding by himself would take 25 hours to do all 8 bookshelves. Ms Fu can organise 2 bookshelves in 7 hours. Mrs Falconer can take 11 hours to organise 3 bookshelves.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Combined rate}&=\frac{8}{25}+\frac{2}{7}+\frac{3}{11}\\\text{Combined rate}&=\frac{1691}{1925}\text{ bookshelves/hour}\\\text{Time for 8 bookshelves}&=8\div\frac{1691}{1925}\\\text{Time for 8 bookshelves}&=\frac{15400}{1691}\text{ hours}\\\text{Time in minutes}&=\frac{15400}{1691}\times60\\\text{Time in minutes}&=\frac{924000}{1691}\text{ minutes}\\\text{Time in minutes}&\approx546\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$
Therefore, they take **9 hours 6 minutes**, to the nearest minute.

inlines.text: Usually when working with rates, we only use two units.

Identify the three quantities in the question.

Convert units to be the same, and to the unit wanted by the question.
A common application is drip rates for medication, important for doctors and nurses.

inlines.text: Calculate how long it will take to deliver 800 mL at 20 drops/min if there are 25 drops/mL.

answer.worked:
Quantities: volume, time and drops.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{Time}}{\text{Volume}}&=\frac{\text{Time}}{\text{Drops}}\times\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Volume}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{800\text{ mL}}&=\frac{1\text{ min}}{20\text{ drops}}\times\frac{25\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{800\text{ mL}}&=\frac{25\text{ min}}{20\text{ mL}}\\x&=800\times\frac{25}{20}\\x&=1000\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$

If there are 16 drops/mL, how long will it take to deliver the required dose?

answer.worked:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{Time}}{\text{Volume}} &= \frac{\text{Time}}{\text{Drops}}\times\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Volume}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{800\text{ mL}} &= \frac{1\text{ min}}{25\text{ drops}}\times\frac{16\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{800\text{ mL}} &= \frac{16\text{ min}}{25\text{ mL}}\\x &= \frac{800\times16}{25}\\x &= 512\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
A patient needs 0.75 g of medicine per day. Pills contain 125 mg each and cost 75 c per pill.
What is the annual cost of medicine, in dollars?

answer.worked:
Quantities: medicine, time, pills and cost. Use 365 days in a year.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Time}}&=\frac{\text{Medicine}}{\text{Time}}\times\frac{\text{Pills}}{\text{Medicine}}\times\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Pills}}\\
\frac{\$x}{1\text{ year}}&=\frac{0.75\text{ g}}{1\text{ day}}\times\frac{1\text{ pill}}{125\text{ mg}}\times\frac{75\text{ c}}{1\text{ pill}}\\
\frac{\$x}{1\text{ year}}&=\frac{0.75\text{ g}}{(1\div365)\text{ years}}\times\frac{1\text{ pill}}{(125\div1000)\text{ g}}\times\frac{\$0.75}{1\text{ pill}}\\
\frac{\$x}{1\text{ year}}&=\$1642.50/\text{yr}
\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: A factory produces 25 widgets in 4 minutes. Each widget requires 15 g of plastic.
Plastic costs $3.20 per kg. What is the cost per hour, in dollars?

answer.worked:
$w$ denotes widgets.

$$\begin{align*}
\frac{\text{cost}}{\text{time}}&=\frac{\text{widgets}}{\text{time}}\times\frac{\text{plastic}}{\text{widget}}\times\frac{\text{cost}}{\text{plastic}}\\
\frac{\$x}{1\text{ hour}}&=\frac{25\text{ w}}{4\text{ min}}\times\frac{15\text{ g}}{1\text{ w}}\times\frac{\$3.20}{1\text{ kg}}\\
\frac{\$x}{1\text{ hour}}&=\frac{25\text{ w}}{(4\div60)\text{ h}}\times\frac{(15\div1000)\text{ kg}}{1\text{ w}}\times\frac{\$3.20}{1\text{ kg}}\\
x&=18
\end{align*}$$

The cost is $\$18/\text{h}$.

Interpret and construct distance–time graphs from authentic data

Rate: Compares quantities with different units (e.g., distance / time).

entries.description:
A river is flowing downstream at a rate of 1 km/h.
In still water Portia can swim at a rate of 2 km/h.
Portia dives into the river and swims downstream, then turns around and swims back to the starting point, taking 0.5 hours in total.
How far did she swim?

presentation.responseSpace: Open working space beneath the prompt; physical dimensions uncertain.
presentation.requiredInterpretation: The supplied answer identifies the requested distance as the total outward and return distance.

entries.description:
Downstream speed: 2 + 1 = 3 km/h
Upstream speed: 2 − 1 = 1 km/h
Let the distance swum downstream be d km. The return distance is also d km.
Time downstream + Time upstream = 0.5 h
Using t = d/s
d/3 + d/1 = 0.5
4d/3 = 0.5
d = 0.375 km
Total distance swum = 2d = 0.75 km = 750 m

entries.description: Calculating Speed in Distance-Time Graphs

Speed on a distance-time graph
These graphs show distance from the origin. Since speed is distance travelled divided by time taken, we calculate speed from a distance-time graph by doing:
speed = |change in y|/change in x
So, speed is the magnitude of the gradient of the line segment.

entries.description: Related Rates

Related Rates Problems
Usually when working with rates, we only use two units.
Sometimes a question will give a third unit (or more).
To solve these problems:
1. Identify the three quantities in the question.
2. Set up a related rate equation.
\[\frac{\text{Quantity 1}}{\text{Quantity 2}}=\frac{\text{Quantity 1}}{\text{Quantity 3}}\times\frac{\text{Quantity 3}}{\text{Quantity 2}}\]
3. Substitute given information.
The scenario will always give two of the rates.
4. Convert units to be the same, and to the unit wanted by the question.
5. Simplify and solve the equation.
A common application is drip rates for medication, important for doctors and nurses.
